location.section: first vārttika, discussed in the Mahābhāṣya's Paspaśā

paraphrase: Since word, meaning and their relation are established (siddha) — as known from the world, where words are used to convey meanings — grammar makes a restriction for the sake of dharma, as in worldly and Vedic matters.
notes: Patañjali glosses 'siddha' as a synonym of 'eternal'. Philosophy of language → U31. Phase-B spot check: wording/locator matched against the local GRETIL/DCS e-text in sources_raw/ (not a formal Phase-C sourcing check).

checks.note: Mahābhāṣya, Paspaśā (pas_10): 'katham punar idaṃ bhagavataḥ pāṇiner ācāryasya lakṣaṇaṃ pravṛttam | siddhe śabdārthasambandhe … nityaparyāyavācī siddhaśabdaḥ'. Paraphrase and note agree.
